Done, with a correction to a stale claim that sent me looking.

The builder ALREADY handled key rollover -- candidate iteration (PKIX-lwr9.4.1) fixed it -- but had no test, and pkix-difftest/baseline-limbo-analysis.md still described build_first_valid_path as unable to do it, because the limbo corpus is out of tree and the baseline was never re-run. The only statement anywhere about this behaviour was a stale one saying it was broken. Doc corrected: rfc5280::nc::permitted-self-issued is expected to be Agreement on a re-run, not StricterThanWild.

Added pkix-path-builder/tests/key_rollover.rs, 4 tests, reusing pkix-path's issue-11 fixtures rather than generating new ones (dependency on PKIX-xj81.1 removed; reasoning recorded there). Both halves now exercise the same bytes, so they cannot drift.

Mutation testing caught two false claims in my own first draft:
- A test named '...not just the shortest one' survived mutating the candidate loop to single-shot. build_first_valid_path builds its PathCandidates WITH a verifier, which filters the one-cert candidate out before validate_path sees it -- so there is no iteration to test. Renamed to what it does pin: the chain is built under a same-name anchor. Added a positive control that the rollover CA is load-bearing.
- The forged-anchor tests are satisfied by signed_by OR validate_path alone; mutating out either leaves them green. Defence in depth rather than a weak assertion, but it does not localise a regression, and the test now says so.
